q: Which of the following best describes software?
options: The physical parts of a computer
Programs, instructions and associated information used to perform computer tasks
Only the files stored on a hard disk
The electrical power supplied to a computer
explain: Software is the set of programs, instructions and related information that tells a computer what to do. Hardware is the physical part.

q: A functional component that performs a particular job, and which together with others can form an application, is called a:
explain: A module is a functional component that does a specific job. Several cooperating modules can form an application, though a module is not universally the smallest software unit.

q: The original instructions written by a programmer are known as:
explain: Source code is what the programmer writes. Object code and machine code are produced later by translation.

q: Which program combines object files and required libraries into a single linked output?
explain: The linker joins object files and libraries. The loader only places the finished program in memory to run it.

q: Which of the following places a program in memory and prepares it to run?
explain: The loader loads the executable into memory and prepares it for execution.

q: Which of the following statements about the .exe extension is correct?
options: It is used by every kind of software
It is a common Windows executable extension, but not all software uses it
It is used only for image files
explain: .exe means executable and is common on Windows, but other software (and other systems) use different formats.

q: A program that is currently being executed, together with its state and resources, is called a:
explain: A program is stored instructions; a process is an executing instance of that program.

q: Who is widely recognised as the first computer programmer for her work on Babbage's Analytical Engine?
explain: Ada Lovelace wrote notes and an algorithm for Babbage's Analytical Engine and is widely regarded as the first programmer.

q: Which of the following is a drawing app found in the traditional Accessories group of a PC?
explain: Paint is a drawing app. Word is a word processor and Excel is a spreadsheet.

q: Which of the following is NOT system software?
explain: A spreadsheet is application software used for a user task. Drivers, operating systems and utilities manage or support the system.

q: MS-DOS is an example of:
explain: MS-DOS is an operating system, which makes it system software, not application software.

q: Which software provides the interface that lets the operating system communicate with a printer?
explain: A device driver gives the OS a way to talk to specific hardware such as printers, graphics cards or network adapters.

q: Which of the following tools examines file-system or drive problems?
explain: Disk checking tools look for file-system or drive errors. Compression saves space, backup copies data, and antivirus fights malware.

q: Defragmentation is the process of:
options: Reorganising scattered file fragments on a hard disk for efficient access
explain: Defragmentation rearranges existing data so each file's pieces sit together. Deleting unnecessary files is Disk Cleanup.

q: Which statement correctly separates Disk Cleanup from defragmentation?
options: Disk Cleanup rearranges data and defragmentation deletes it
Disk Cleanup deletes unnecessary data while defragmentation rearranges existing data
explain: Cleanup removes selected temporary and unneeded files; defragmentation only reorganises data that is kept.

q: Which technique does Windows commonly use when optimising an SSD, instead of classic defragmentation?
explain: Windows treats HDDs and SSDs differently; SSD optimisation commonly uses TRIM.

q: Software built for a particular defined job, such as payroll or ticket reservation, is called:
explain: Special-purpose application software handles a defined task, while general-purpose software serves common needs.

q: ERP stands for:
explain: ERP is Enterprise Resource Planning, software that integrates finance, purchasing, inventory and human resources.

q: Which statement about ERP and SAP is correct?
options: ERP is a company and SAP is a software category
ERP and SAP are the same thing
ERP is a software category and SAP is a company supplying business software
SAP is an operating system and ERP is a compiler
explain: ERP is a category of software; SAP is a company whose products include ERP applications.

q: Software that serves a particular industry or profession, such as hospital-management or hotel-management systems, is called:
explain: Vertical (industry-specific or niche) software is built for one industry. Horizontal software, like a word processor, serves many industries.

q: Finacle, a banking software example of vertical software, was developed by:
explain: Finacle is banking software developed by Infosys. Bacs, by contrast, is a UK payment system and not a core banking package.

q: Which of the following is a UK payment system supporting Direct Debit and Direct Credit?
explain: Bacs is a UK payment system. It is not a core banking software package like Finacle.

q: Which of the following is an example of open source software?
explain: Firefox is open source. Microsoft Office, Tally and Avast are closed source examples.

q: Which statement about open source software is correct?
options: It must always be free of charge
Its licence makes source code available and permits use, modification and redistribution under stated conditions
It can never be sold commercially
It can be modified by anyone without any skill
explain: Open source is about source-code rights under a licence. It can be free or sold, and modifying it may still need programming skill.

q: Software distributed for evaluation, with payment expected or required for continued use or extra features, is called:
explain: Shareware is for evaluation, after which payment is expected. Freeware has no purchase price.

q: Software that repeatedly shows pop-up reminders asking the user to register, buy or pay is known as:
explain: Nagware, also called annoyware or begware, nags users with repeated reminders.

q: EULA stands for:
explain: EULA is the End User License Agreement, the terms that govern how an end user may install, copy and use the software.

q: Which statement about public-domain software is correct?
options: It is not protected by copyright, whereas freeware and open source can still be copyrighted
It is the same as freeware
It is the same as open source software
It is software protected by a EULA
explain: Public-domain software has no copyright protection. Freeware and open-source software are free to get but still copyrighted.

q: Which translator converts assembly-language instructions into machine-code object output?
explain: An assembler handles assembly language. Converting a high-level language into assembly is a compiler task.

q: In Java, which component executes bytecode using interpretation and, in many implementations, just-in-time compilation?
explain: The Java compiler produces bytecode, and the Java Virtual Machine (JVM) runs it. This is why Java is the usual example of compilation plus interpretation.

q: Which tool helps inspect program execution and locate defects, but is NOT a language translator?
explain: A debugger is a separate tool for finding defects. Compilers, interpreters and assemblers are the translators.

q: Which malware self-replicates and can spread without attaching itself to a host file?
explain: A worm spreads on its own. A virus needs an infected host file or program to run.

q: A targeted fix released for defects, vulnerabilities or behaviour in software is called a:
explain: A patch is a targeted fix. An upgrade is a move to a newer or more capable version, and a bug is the defect itself.

q: Software stored in non-volatile memory to control a device's basic functions, such as BIOS/UEFI, is called:
explain: Firmware lives in non-volatile memory such as ROM, EEPROM or flash and controls basic device operation.

q: Which software is often called the 'glue' because it connects applications, components, clients, servers and data sources?
explain: Middleware provides shared services that link applications and other components together.
